A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same StableMaterials work. All 11 pages of each version, including equations, tables, figures and appended qualitative results, are readable and support comparison across renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original material-generation results, comparative examples, VAE reconstruction RMSE, ablations and inference-time measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds a quantitative generation-quality comparison using CLIP Score and CLIP-IQA.

M1.justification: The single-encoder VAE, shared texture/material latent representation, semi-supervised adversarial training, feature rolling, latent consistency model and SDEdit refinement remain unchanged. Section 3 and Figure 3 clarify the existing procedure without establishing an algorithmic revision.

E1.justification: Both retain 6,198 materials from MatSynth and Deschaintre et al., plus 4,000 SDXL textures generated from 200 prompts. Image/text conditioning and in-domain/out-of-domain material coverage remain the same; the new quantitative evaluation stays within existing task coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 6 retains MatFuse, MatGen and MaterialPalette for image prompting; Figure 7 retains MatFuse, MatGen and Substance 3D Sampler for text prompting. The new quantitative Table 1 evaluates the same comparator set already used in the text-prompting comparison.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 introduces a quantitative generation-quality protocol using 80 text-conditioned generations, CLIP Score and CLIP-IQA. Table 1 specifies the latter's high-quality/low-quality contrastive pair. This substantially extends the earlier visual baseline evaluation, while existing training splits, budgets and inference settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The VAE and semi-supervision ablations are retained. v3 Figure 9 removes the stone refinement example from v2 Figure 9 and replaces v2 Figure 10's tortoise-shell high-resolution comparison with brickwork. The refinement and scale-consistency questions and principal findings remain the same.

E5.justification: Both retain the fixed-seed inference setup in Section 4.2. Neither reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new quantitative comparison supplies point scores; its 80 generations are an evaluation sample count, not reported repeated-run uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v3 Table 1 adds CLIP Score results of 26.2, 28.8, 24.9 and 29.6, and CLIP-IQA results of 0.52, 0.66, 0.71 and 0.70 for MatFuse, MatGen, Sampler and StableMaterials, respectively. StableMaterials leads CLIP Score, while Sampler leads CLIP-IQA. These are newly reported comparisons; retained VAE RMSE and inference timings are unchanged. Some high-resolution qualitative examples are replaced or removed.

T1.justification: Equation (1) replaces the comma between actual and predicted noise inside each norm with subtraction, correcting the formal squared-error expression. This limited mathematical correction agrees with v2's accompanying description of noise comparison; no new theorem, proof or derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The core contributions remain semi-supervised material generation, knowledge transfer from large image models, feature rolling and claimed state-of-the-art generation quality. Fast, tileable, high-resolution output and reduced reliance on annotated data remain central claims. The quantitative comparison adds support without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 adds arguments that predominantly supervised training avoids mode collapse and adversarial alignment counters shading artifacts. Section 4.3 motivates CLIP-based evaluation. Section 5 newly states that generation remains limited to classes represented in unannotated data. The earlier circular-padding failure explanation in Section 3.4 is removed.

D1.justification: v2's public-availability statement and project URL become a future-release promise without the URL. v3 newly documents non-overlap between evaluation and training prompts, without establishing a changed split. It removes the MatFuse-on-MatSynth specification and the footnote identifying author-provided MatGen samples. Main hardware and hyperparameter disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for CLIPScore, CLIP-IQA, FID and Inception Score, and explicitly distinguishes its domain-transfer distillation from adversarial methods aimed at faster generation. ControlMat's change from a 2023 preprint citation to its 2024 publication identifies the same work.

P1.justification: Section 3 is extensively rewritten, including a numbered explanation of the loss roles and separate supervised-loss, adversarial-loss and discriminator paragraphs. Results, ablation discussion and the conclusion are also substantially rewritten. This is a broad explanatory revision despite retention of the main section order and scientific procedure.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is redrawn from a column-sized diagram into a full-width training flow showing noising, denoising and loss connections. A new quantitative Table 1 is inserted, and former Figures 9–10 become Figure 9a–b with fewer and partly replaced examples, substantially reorganizing the ablation page. Appended generation figures retain their examples and are renumbered.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens previously visual generation comparisons with quantitative evidence, clarifies the training procedure, corrects Equation (1) and states a meaningful coverage limitation. These gains are limited by the 80-generation CLIP evaluation's lack of uncertainty reporting and losses in documentation, including the project link and comparator provenance. Overall, the evidence and clarity improve modestly.
